title: Now Sinks the Fiery Orb of Day
description: Now Sinks the Fiery Orb of Day in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Latin hymns of the early Church for Hymns of the Early Church (London, 1896), headed “Saturday Evening”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now sinks the fie-ry orb of day— O One in Three, E-ter-nal Light, O Three in One, for ev-er bright, Shine in our dark-ened minds, we pray.

lines: Now sinks the fiery orb of day—
O One in Three, Eternal Light,
O Three in One, for ever bright,
Shine in our darkened minds, we pray.
When morning breaks, our songs we raise;
When evening falls, we still adore;
When morn and eve shall come no more,
In mercy grant us still to praise.
All praises to the Father be,
All praise to the Eternal Son,
And to the Spirit, Three in One,

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Early Church (1896)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Latin, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Early Church; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
